The reconciliation is done and the memo has been submitted. Summary of what I did:

**Root cause of the USD 10,450 vs EUR 7,800 difference**

| US 1400 component | Support | USD |
|---|---|---|
| ICI-DE-01 Feb software recharge, EUR 7,800 @1.08 | DOC-0125 | 8,424 |
| ICI-DE-02 Mar CI/CD tooling recharge, EUR 500 @1.10 | DOC-0190 | 550 |
| Remeasurement of EUR 8,300 to 1.10 | DOC-0204 | 156 |
| **Supported subtotal (EUR 8,300 × 1.10)** | | **9,130** |
| JE-00306 "IC adj DE per call" (manual, no document) | none | 1,320 |
| **Total** | | **10,450** |

**Booked on DE's side (supported):** JE-00309 — Dr 6200 / Cr 2300 EUR 500 for ICI-DE-02, invoice DOC-0190 attached, dated 3/18 in the open period. DE 2300 now verified at EUR 8,300, which at the March policy rate equals the USD 9,130 of supported US receivable exactly.

**Escalated (not booked):** EXC-001 for the USD 1,320 (~EUR 1,200). JE-00306 has no invoice, agreement, or written confirmation anywhere in the document store, no related cash movement, and was even excluded from the US's own FX remeasurement. Per policy §2/§11, I did not have DE book it to force agreement. The controller needs to either provide support (DE will then record it) or reverse JE-00306 on the US side.

**Checklist:** DE intercompany reconciliation marked complete; US marked blocked pending EXC-001.

One thing worth noting for the controller: I confirmed there is no US–DE loan in play (US 1410's USD 200k is the UK loan under DOC-0016; DE 2400 is zero), so the difference is entirely in the trading intercompany accounts.
